summary: Recover from round-2 regression by removing confident-primary fallback and replacing primitive attention with SDPA
rationale: Round 2 showed 52% step time regression (30s -> 46s) due to confident-primary fallback
The fallback caused excessive token dropping (43123) and poor load balance (CV=3.42)
Removing the fallback restores standard top-2 routing behavior
SDPA attention is more efficient than primitive MultiheadAttention with manual masks
expected_effects: Step time should return to near round-1 levels (~30s)
Attention computation should be faster with SDPA
risks: May not fully recover round-1 performance if other factors changed
SDPA behavior may differ slightly from primitive attention on edge cases
